subject: Reasoning
description: Statement-conclusion, syllogism-style implications, only conclusion which follows

questions.stem: Statement: 'All roses are flowers. All flowers fade.' Which conclusion necessarily follows?

options.option_text: Some flowers are not roses, regardless of fading
All roses fade in due course of time
Only roses fade, not other flowers
Flowers do not fade if they are roses

questions.explanation: Transitivity of universal categorical statements: All A are B; All B are C → All A are C. So all roses are flowers and all flowers fade → all roses fade. Distractor 1 may be true in fact but doesn't FOLLOW from the given statements (statements don't say there exist non-rose flowers). Distractor 3 reverses the universal. Distractor 4 contradicts the conclusion.

questions.stem: Statement: 'Some doctors are surgeons. All surgeons attend conferences.' Which conclusion necessarily follows?

options.option_text: All doctors attend conferences regularly
Some doctors attend conferences regularly
All conference attendees are surgeons
No doctors attend any conferences ever

questions.explanation: Some doctors are surgeons; all surgeons attend → those doctor-surgeons attend → SOME doctors attend conferences. Cannot conclude ALL doctors attend (we only know SOME are surgeons). Distractor 1 is too strong. Distractor 3 reverses (all surgeons attend ≠ all attendees are surgeons). Distractor 4 contradicts.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'No politician is honest. Some lawyers are politicians.' Which conclusion necessarily follows?

options.option_text: All lawyers are dishonest because of their profession
Some lawyers are not honest because they are politicians
All politicians are also lawyers in this scenario
No lawyer can ever take part in active politics

questions.explanation: Some lawyers are politicians, and no politician is honest. Therefore those lawyer-politicians are not honest → SOME lawyers are not honest. Cannot conclude ALL lawyers are dishonest. Distractor 1 too strong. Distractor 3 reverses 'some'. Distractor 4 contradicts the second statement.

questions.stem: Statement: 'If it rains, the match will be cancelled. The match was not cancelled.' What can be deduced?

options.option_text: It rained heavily during the match
It did not rain during the match
The match was cancelled for another reason
Rain has no effect on cancelling matches

questions.explanation: MODUS TOLLENS: 'If P then Q' + 'NOT Q' → 'NOT P'. If rain → cancelled. Match wasn't cancelled (NOT Q) → it didn't rain (NOT P). Distractor 1 contradicts the deduction. Distractor 3 wrongly assumes the match was cancelled. Distractor 4 misreads the conditional structure.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Statement: 'All students study hard. Ravi studies hard.' What CAN be concluded?

options.option_text: Ravi is definitely a student in some school
Ravi may or may not be a student
Ravi studies harder than other students do
Ravi is not a student in any school

questions.explanation: AFFIRMING THE CONSEQUENT FALLACY: 'all students study hard' means S → H, but knowing H doesn't imply S (other people may study hard too). Ravi may or may not be a student. Distractor 1 falls into the affirming-the-consequent trap. Distractors 3 and 4 are unsupported.

questions.stem: Statement: 'All cats are mammals. No mammal lays eggs (excluding monotremes).' Which conclusion follows for cats?

options.option_text: Cats lay eggs in some habitats
Cats do not lay eggs in any habitat
Cats sometimes belong to the bird family
Cats are reptiles in cold climates only

questions.explanation: All cats are mammals; no mammal lays eggs (with the parenthetical excluding monotremes like platypus). Therefore no cat lays eggs. Direct categorical syllogism. Distractor 1 contradicts. Distractor 3 — cats are not birds. Distractor 4 — cats are not reptiles.

questions.stem: Statement: 'Either Ravi or Sita won the contest. Sita did not win the contest.' What follows?

options.option_text: Both Ravi and Sita lost the contest
Ravi won the contest
Neither of them participated in the contest
The contest was cancelled before completion

questions.explanation: DISJUNCTIVE SYLLOGISM: 'P or Q' + 'NOT Q' → 'P'. 'Either Ravi or Sita won' + 'Sita did not' → Ravi won. Distractor 1 contradicts the original 'either won'. Distractors 3, 4 import unsupported claims.
